title: Dry sweeping and mopping: route order, bucket position and drying
audience: Cleaners who dry sweep and mop hard floors in commercial, residential and strata work.
learningOutcomes: Plan the working order so that you finish at the exit and do not walk over cleaned floor.
Dry sweep with a dustpan and brush and place the waste in the bag the business specifies.
Park the bucket on the already-mopped side and avoid carrying dirty water across cleaned floor.
Keep warning signs in place until the floor is completely dry.

instruction.heading: Clear the floor first
instruction.body: Before you dry sweep or mop, remove moveable objects from the floor area, such as bins, chairs, mats and loose cables. Set them where they will not block the route. Anything left on the floor will either stop the mop or be missed, and it leaves a line of soil under the mop head. If an object cannot be moved safely, report it rather than working around it blind.

instruction.heading: Plan the route from the far end
instruction.body: Work from the point furthest from the exit back toward the exit. This keeps you from walking over floor you have already finished, and it leaves you a clean, dry route out. In a large room, divide the floor into sections and finish each section before starting the next. Do not leave a section half-wet across a route that people must use.

instruction.heading: Dry sweeping
instruction.body: Dry sweeping lifts loose dust and debris before any moisture is applied, which stops the soil being smeared into a film. Sweep in the direction the procedure sets, gather the waste into a pile, and lift it with a dustpan and brush. Place the waste into the refuse bag the business specifies. Do not sweep debris into a corner to deal with later. Sharp or hazardous items are not swept in with ordinary debris. Handle them as the procedure directs.

instruction.heading: Mopping and the position of the bucket
instruction.body: Park the bucket on the already-mopped side, moving it forward as you progress, and never set it over floor you have not yet mopped. Dip the mop, wring it to the level the procedure sets, and mop in overlapping passes. Change the water when it is visibly dirty, rather than spreading soil across a larger area. Do not let the mop head dry out between passes, and do not leave solution pooled on the floor.

instruction.heading: Warning signs and drying
instruction.body: Place a warning sign wherever a wet floor creates a fall risk, and keep it in place until the floor is completely dry, not just until you have left the area. A floor often looks dry while the surface under a shoe is still slippery, especially in corners, at edges and under mats. Where drying takes a long time, rope off the route or use a barrier. Check the surface before you remove the sign.

instruction.heading: Finishing the floor
instruction.body: When the floor is finished, return the bucket and equipment to the allocated place, not to the walkway. Record the floor area completed and whether the drying check was met before the sign came down.

procedure: Place warning signs where a wet floor will create a fall risk.
Remove moveable objects from the floor area, and report any that cannot be moved safely.
Plan the route from the point furthest from the exit back toward the exit.
Dry sweep, lifting the waste with a dustpan and brush into the refuse bag the business specifies.
Park the bucket on the already-mopped side, mop in overlapping passes, and change the water when it is dirty.
Leave the warning signs in place until the floor is completely dry, then remove them and store the equipment.

workedExamples.situation: You mop a corridor that has one exit. You start near the exit and the bucket sits in the middle of the wet floor, between you and the far end.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What are the two errors, and how do you correct them?
workedExamples.reasoning: The route runs toward the exit, so you finish at the far end, away from the exit, and you have walked back over floor you have cleaned. The bucket is set on floor that still needs cleaning. Reverse the route so that you start at the far end and work back toward the exit, keeping the bucket on the already-mopped side.

workedExamples.situation: From the doorway, the floor looks dry, so you remove the warning sign straight away.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What check should you make before you move the sign?
workedExamples.reasoning: Walk the surface, or at least check the corners, edges and the area under any mat, to confirm the floor is completely dry before you remove the sign. A distant look is not enough. Removing the sign too early can leave a slip risk for the next person.

workedExamples.situation: While sweeping, you find a piece of broken glass in the dustpan with the ordinary debris.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the glass?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop and do not tip the glass into the general bag by hand. Put on the gloves the job requires, collect the glass using the sharps method in the procedure, and tell the supervisor. If you cannot tell where the glass came from, report the area so that it can be checked.

equipmentAndPpe: Dry sweeping broom and dustpan with brush
Refuse bag of the colour and type the business specifies
Mop head and bucket, with the warning sign in place
Gloves for sharp or broken items

commonErrors.error: Working toward the exit, so that the route out is cleaned last and crossed while wet.
commonErrors.prevention: Start at the point furthest from the exit and finish at the exit.

commonErrors.error: Pushing the bucket ahead onto floor that still needs cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Park the bucket on the already-mopped side at all times.

commonErrors.error: Removing the sign because the floor looks dry from a distance.
commonErrors.prevention: Check that the whole surface, including corners and edges, is completely dry before removing the sign.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping debris into a corner to deal with later.
commonErrors.prevention: Collect the waste into a pile and into the specified bag as you go.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wet floors create a slip hazard. Warning signs and drying checks are controls set by the business.
Sharp or hazardous waste is handled under the business's waste procedure and any applicable state or territory waste rules.
Chemical use follows the product label and the safety data sheet.

qualityStandard: The floor is cleared of moveable objects before work starts, and no object is left under the mop.
The route runs from the furthest point to the exit, with no walking over cleaned floor.
Waste is collected into the specified bag, with no debris left in corners.
Warning signs are removed only after the floor is completely dry.
documentationEvidence: Floor checklist showing the area completed, sign placement and the drying check.
Incident record for any slip, spill or broken item.
summary: Clear the floor, then plan the route from the far end toward the exit.
Dry sweep first, and bag the waste as the business specifies.
Park the bucket on the already-mopped side, and change dirty water.
Signs stay in place until the floor is completely dry.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should you start mopping a corridor that has one exit?
options: At the exit, so that you can see the whole floor
In the middle, working in both directions at once
At the point furthest from the exit, working back toward it

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should the mop bucket sit while you mop?
options: Ahead of you, to reach it

knowledgeChecks.question: When may a wet-floor warning sign be removed?
options: Once you have left the area and started on the next room
When the floor is completely dry, including corners and edges
When the floor looks dry from the doorway

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the lesson say dry sweeping is done before any moisture is applied?
options: It removes the need for a mop
It stops the soil being smeared into a film
